what: NEXT-9 (2026-10-26): the C BCIRQ8 decoder's next two kernel levers after DECODE-ROW, each prototyped with every value the same and measured, neither taken; records only, no runtime change. Q8-HOIST: the vector matvecs' x times a group's scale formed once a row and group (code*(x*s) for x*(code*s), the same bits wherever x*s is exact), every such product checked and a call that formed an inexact one computed again by the committed kernel (q8_hoist.patch). Without the check the hoist runs the block matvec at x0.852-0.960 of its time; with it the prototype is x0.995-1.144 at the 860K decoder's shapes (x1.042-1.109 over the decoder's 28 matvecs in order) and x0.967-1.060 at TinyLlama's. In one binary with the matvec's path chosen at run time the prototype makes a token x0.937-0.957 of its time under clang and x0.967-0.978 under GCC, the committed kernel's copy at addresses of its own x0.997-1.012 and x0.971-1.006; the gain is this host's clock. A dependent add chain run between the matvecs at a decode's duty cycle reads the committed kernel's AVX-512 matvecs lengthening the core's cycle x1.202 (clang, the median of 3 runs) against none, and the prototype's leaving it x0.946 and x0.958 (GCC) as long as the committed kernel's, in x1.027 and x1.039 of its cycles. The clock answers the prototype's per-group checks, not its multiplies: the same kernel without them (the ceiling) leaves clang's cycle x1.002 while taking x0.884 of the committed kernel's cycles -- the kernel's own gain, a token x0.917-0.941 (x0.925-0.965 under GCC, whose build of it raises the clock too). Not taken: the prototype's gain is the clock answering its checks, through a kernel that is itself slower. The ceiling, exact here because every byte is compared, sizes Q8-BOUND: the hoist with exactness proved once a call. Q8-ROWS2: the head's row dots sixteen rows a step in two interleaved blocks, x1.050 (clang) and x1.043 (GCC) at the 860K decoder's head and x0.992 and x1.061 at TinyLlama's head of 32,000 rows.
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.30GHz, 4 vCPU (4 cores, one thread each; AVX-512F, AMX), 2 MiB of L2 a core, 260 MiB of L3; Linux 6.18; clang 18.1.3 and GCC 13.3 (-std=c11 -O2 -ffp-contract=off, the qualification's flags); Python 3.11.15
